parliament.name: Cortes de Castilla-La Mancha
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

regions.name: Canary Islands
regions.identity_basis: Atlantic archipelago off Northwest Africa with a distinct Canarian Spanish dialect, Guanche pre-colonial substrate, and special fiscal/economic autonomy regime (REF); included as an outlying autonomous unit alongside Portugal's Azores and Madeira per project framing.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAC), Canarias NUTS-2 ES70

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Las Palmas de Gran Canaria — metro ~700k, major Atlantic port and cultural capital, twin-capital arrangement with Santa Cruz de Tenerife
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism (dominant), port/container transshipment, banana export agriculture, growing renewable-energy and tech sector
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Canarian identity and special fiscal autonomy status, integrated within Spain as an outermost EU region

autarky.rationale: Volcanic-island geography and near-total tourism/import dependence give structurally low water and food self-sufficiency; desalination and import logistics are well developed but represent dependency rather than autarky.

rationales.water: Volcanic-island geography forces near-total reliance on desalination — a dependency, not autarky.
rationales.food: Banana-export monoculture and import-heavy tourism supply chains give low self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Isolated island grids rely on imported fuel oil despite growing wind/solar investment.

pole.note: De facto co-capital arrangement (seat of government alternates/splits institutions between the two).

parliament.name: Parlamento de Canarias
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

regions.name: Balearic Islands
regions.identity_basis: Mediterranean archipelago with Catalan-family Balearic dialect (mallorquí, menorquí, eivissenc) and a distinct island identity shaped by mass tourism; included as an outlying unit alongside the Canary Islands.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (IBESTAT), Illes Balears NUTS-2 ES53

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Palma de Mallorca — metro ~470k, dominant island capital and Mediterranean tourism/yachting hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism and hospitality overwhelmingly dominant, supplemented by nautical services and Mallorcan agriculture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Balearic-Catalan linguistic identity, integrated within Spain, tourism-driven economy occasionally in tension with residents (housing-cost protests)

autarky.rationale: Small, water-stressed islands almost entirely dependent on imported food, fuel, and (in peak season) desalinated water to serve tourist populations many multiples of resident population.

rationales.water: Small, water-stressed islands depend heavily on desalination for peak tourist-season demand.
rationales.food: Near-total food import dependence to serve a resident-plus-tourist population many multiples of residents.
rationales.energy: Fuel imports dominate; limited domestic renewable buildout relative to demand.

sources: IBESTAT (Institut d'Estadística de les Illes Balears)

parliament.name: Parlament de les Illes Balears
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

regions.name: Lisbon
regions.name_local: Grande Lisboa / Área Metropolitana de Lisboa
regions.identity_basis: Capital-region identity centered on the Tagus estuary; national political, financial, and cultural seat, distinct from the Porto-centered north per the mandated Porto/Lisbon split.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE Portugal), sum of Grande Lisboa (PT1A) + Península de Setúbal (PT1B) + Oeste e Vale do Tejo (PT1D, ~400,000, approximate — absorbed in schema v2 to close a mainland-Portugal coverage gap; PT1D has no independent identity or urban center per the original zone assessment and functions as a Lisbon commuter/agricultural buffer, not a distinct cultural unit).

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Lisbon — metro ~2.9M, national capital and largest urban agglomeration
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance, tourism, growing tech/startup sector, Atlantic port and logistics, public administration
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: capital identity distinct from Porto/Norte per mandated split; no separatism, standard capital-region dynamics

autarky.rationale: Best national transport and healthcare infrastructure as capital region; food and energy self-sufficiency low given import dependence typical of a dense coastal megacity.

rationales.water: Tagus-basin reservoirs meet normal demand but leave little drought margin for a dense capital region.
rationales.food: Import-dependent coastal megacity with minimal agricultural hinterland of its own.
rationales.energy: No significant domestic generation; grid-imported power typical of a capital-region economy.

sources: AML (Área Metropolitana de Lisboa) planning documents

reach.note: As national capital, Lisbon's institutional and service reach extends nominally across mainland Portugal, beyond the metropolitan-area boundary used for this cultural unit.

parliament.note: Mainland Portugal is a unitary state with no regional parliaments (unlike the Azores/Madeira autonomous regions); unit justified on capital-region/coverage grounds, not the parliament rule.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 PT1 (Continente) merges Norte with Lisbon and the rest of mainland Portugal; split here per the mandated Porto/Norte ≠ Lisbon decision.
regions.name: Porto / Norte
regions.identity_basis: Historic core of the Portuguese nation (the country's name derives from Portus Cale/Porto); distinct northern industrial and Douro-wine identity, mandated as separate from Lisbon per project brief.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE Portugal), Norte NUTS-2 PT11

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Porto — metro ~1.7M, UNESCO historic center, Portugal's second city and industrial/commercial capital of the north
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: textiles and footwear export clusters, Douro Valley port-wine viticulture (UNESCO landscape), automotive supply, tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong northern Portuguese identity distinct from Lisbon-centric national narrative, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Douro Valley agriculture and viticulture plus Atlantic rainfall support strong food and water self-sufficiency; long-standing textile/footwear manufacturing gives above-average clothing self-sufficiency for the dataset.

rationales.water: Atlantic rainfall and the Douro watershed give reliable, ample supply.
rationales.food: Douro Valley agriculture and viticulture give strong self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Douro hydro cascade gives above-average domestic generation for the Portuguese set.

parliament.note: Mainland Portugal unitary structure — no regional parliament; unit justified on cultural/historic-identity and coverage grounds.

regions.name: Algarve
regions.identity_basis: Formerly a separate title within the Portuguese crown ('Kingdom of the Algarve', held distinct from the Kingdom of Portugal until 1910 in royal styling); Moorish-influenced history and a distinct southern coastal culture and (residual) Algarvian dialect.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE Portugal), Algarve NUTS-2 PT15

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Faro — regional capital and airport gateway for the Algarve tourism economy
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism overwhelmingly dominant, supplemented by fishing and citrus agriculture; weakest industrial diversification in the Portuguese set, flagged honestly
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: historic separate 'Kingdom of the Algarve' royal title gives an unusually strong formal-historical basis for distinctness despite the small population

autarky.rationale: Tourism monoculture and seasonal population multiples of residents strain water supply; fishing and citrus give moderate food self-sufficiency but energy and clothing are import-dependent.

rationales.water: Seasonal tourist-population multiples of residents strain a naturally dry Mediterranean-climate coast.
rationales.food: Fishing and citrus give moderate self-sufficiency but tourism-driven imports dominate.
rationales.energy: High solar potential exists but is under-exploited; net importer via mainland grid.

sources: Historical Kingdom of the Algarve constitutional literature

pole.note: Administrative/airport-gateway center; tourism development itself is diffuse along the coast.

parliament.note: Mainland Portugal unitary structure — no regional parliament; unit justified on the historic 'Kingdom of the Algarve' identity basis, not the parliament rule.

regions.name: Azores
regions.identity_basis: Volcanic Atlantic archipelago with full political-administrative autonomy (own regional government and assembly) within Portugal; mandated autonomous outlying unit per global constraints.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE Portugal / SREA), Região Autónoma dos Açores NUTS-2 PT20

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Ponta Delgada — archipelago's largest city and seat of regional government
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: dairy and cattle farming (major Portuguese milk exporter), fishing, whale-watching tourism, geothermal power
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: full autonomous-region status within Portugal, distinct Azorean identity, no independence movement of consequence

autarky.rationale: Volcanic geothermal resources and pasture-based dairy give above-average energy and food self-sufficiency for an island economy; inter-island transportation is the binding constraint across a dispersed nine-island archipelago.

rationales.water: High Atlantic-volcanic rainfall gives ample fresh water across the nine islands.
rationales.food: Pasture-based dairy/cattle farming makes the Azores a major Portuguese milk exporter.
rationales.energy: Geothermal power (São Miguel) gives above-average self-generation for an island economy.

sources: SREA (Serviço Regional de Estatística dos Açores)

pole.note: Nine-island archipelago; Angra do Heroísmo is historic co-capital (UNESCO), Horta a secondary Atlantic-crossing hub.

parliament.name: Assembleia Legislativa da Região Autónoma dos Açores
parliament.note: Full political-administrative autonomy within Portugal, unlike mainland regions.

regions.name: Madeira
regions.identity_basis: Volcanic Atlantic archipelago off Northwest Africa with full political-administrative autonomy within Portugal, added here alongside the Azores by direct analogy — the underlying zone specification named only the Azores as a mandated autonomous outlying unit, but Madeira shares the identical constitutional status (own regional government, own statute of autonomy) and was added on that basis; flagged for the methodology page.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE Portugal / DREM), Região Autónoma da Madeira NUTS-2 PT30

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Funchal — archipelago capital, major Atlantic cruise-tourism port
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism (dominant), Madeira wine export, banana and subtropical agriculture, embroidery handicraft export
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: full autonomous-region status identical to the Azores, distinct Madeiran identity, no independence movement

autarky.rationale: Steep volcanic terrain limits arable land despite fertile soils, capping food self-sufficiency; tourism dependence and island isolation constrain energy and transportation scores similarly to the Azores.

rationales.water: Steep volcanic terrain limits catchment/storage despite fertile soils.
rationales.food: Limited arable land caps output; banana/wine agriculture is real but small-scale.
rationales.energy: Isolated island grid with limited hydro; largely fuel-import dependent.

sources: DREM (Direção Regional de Estatística da Madeira)

parliament.name: Assembleia Legislativa da Região Autónoma da Madeira
parliament.note: Full political-administrative autonomy within Portugal, unlike mainland regions.

conflict_flags.description: Valle d'Aosta/Vallée d'Aoste (ITC2) is a bilingual French-Italian special-autonomy region with its own statute, distinct from Piedmontese identity, folded into this record for population/urban-hub scale (~123,000 residents, no independent metro of dataset-relevant size). Toggleable as a separate micro-region if finer granularity is adopted.

regions.name: Piedmont
regions.identity_basis: Historic core of the Kingdom of Sardinia/House of Savoy that unified Italy; Piedmontese dialect and cuisine (Slow Food origin, Barolo/Barbaresco wine country) distinct from the rest of the Nord-Ovest.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), sum of Piemonte (ITC1) + Valle d'Aosta (ITC2)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Turin — metro ~1.7M, cradle of Italian automotive industry and post-Olympic (2006) design/aerospace hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive (Stellantis/Fiat), aerospace (Thales Alenia, Leonardo), premium wine, precision manufacturing, ICT
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Piedmontese regional identity and cuisine culture, historically the unifying royal house of Italy, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Alpine water resources and premium wine/agriculture support strong food and water scores; historic automotive/aerospace manufacturing base gives resilient, diversified production capacity.

rationales.water: Alpine glacier-fed rivers (Po headwaters) give abundant, reliable supply.
rationales.food: Premium Langhe/Barolo viticulture and Po-plain agriculture give strong self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Alpine hydropower is significant but Turin's automotive/aerospace industrial base still nets an importer.

sources: Regione Piemonte and Valle d'Aosta statutory autonomy documentation

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale del Piemonte
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.special_status: Alpine Occitan and Franco-Provençal (Arpitan) minority-language valleys (upper Susa, Chisone, Po, Pellice, Varaita, Maira, Grana, Stura valleys) plus the region's historic core-of-Savoy identity, per explicit user instruction ('special zone like Monaco'); rendered with a dashed stroke like the other special_status units even though Piedmont as a whole is an ordinary (non-special-statute) Italian region.

regions.name: Liguria
regions.identity_basis: Historic maritime Republic of Genoa; distinct Ligurian dialect and coastal identity along the narrow Riviera; mandated as a separate region per global constraints.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Liguria NUTS-2 ITC3

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Genoa — metro ~800k, Italy's largest port and historic maritime-republic capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: port/maritime logistics, shipbuilding (Fincantieri), precision engineering, coastal tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Ligurian maritime-republic identity, no separatism, mandated standalone status per project brief

autarky.rationale: Narrow coastal geography with limited arable land caps food self-sufficiency; the Port of Genoa gives strong logistics/transportation self-sufficiency for goods flow rather than autarky per se.

rationales.water: Narrow coastal catchments limit storage relative to dense port-city demand.
rationales.food: Minimal arable land on the steep Riviera caps food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Genoa port/refining activity is energy-intensive with little domestic generation to offset it.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Liguria
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Lombardy
regions.identity_basis: Historic Duchy of Milan/Lombard identity; Italy's economic powerhouse and financial capital, with a distinct Lombard dialect substrate and a regionalist (Lega Nord-origin) political current focused on fiscal autonomy rather than secession.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Lombardia NUTS-2 ITC4

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Milan — metro ~3.2M, Italy's financial and fashion capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance, fashion/design, advanced manufacturing, pharma/biotech, publishing/media
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Lombard identity and fiscal-autonomy politics, integrated within Italy, no serious separatism

autarky.rationale: Po Valley irrigation and Alpine watershed give strong water and food scores; Italy's densest transport/logistics network and diversified high-value manufacturing base support resilient shelter/transportation/hygiene-healthcare scores.

rationales.water: Po Valley irrigation and Alpine watershed give strong, reliable supply for Italy's most populous region.
rationales.food: Intensive Po-plain agriculture (rice, dairy) gives solid self-sufficiency despite Milan's dense urban core.
rationales.energy: Alpine hydro plus industrial cogeneration offset part of Italy's densest manufacturing energy load.

reach.note: Milan's metropolitan labor market draws heavily on cross-border commuters (frontalieri) from Swiss Ticino; reach runs opposite the usual capital-hinterland direction (a wealthier neighbor supplying labor to the pole).

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Lombardia
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Veneto
regions.identity_basis: Historic Republic of Venice (La Serenissima); distinct Venetian language/dialect and a modern regionalist current (2017 non-binding autonomy referendum) seeking greater fiscal autonomy within Italy.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Veneto NUTS-2 ITH3

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Venice — globally iconic historic-maritime capital; Verona/Padua as secondary economic hubs
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism, gold/jewelry manufacturing (Vicenza), furniture (Treviso), Prosecco viticulture, leather/footwear
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Venetian regional identity with an active but non-secessionist autonomy movement

autarky.rationale: Po Valley plain and Prosecco hills give solid food self-sufficiency; Venice's lagoon geography creates unique but manageable water/shelter vulnerabilities (acqua alta flooding, MOSE barrier).

rationales.water: Po Valley plain and Dolomite headwaters give solid supply, moderated by Venice's lagoon-specific vulnerabilities.
rationales.food: Po Valley agriculture and Prosecco-hill viticulture give strong self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Limited domestic generation; industrial SME base (Vicenza, Treviso) is a net energy importer.

pole.note: Veneto's 'città diffusa' settlement pattern: Verona/Padua/Vicenza are economically comparable to Venice, which retains symbolic/political centrality.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale del Veneto
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
regions.identity_basis: Special-statute autonomous region with a trilingual heritage (Friulian, Italian, Slovene) and Trieste's distinct Habsburg-port history at the head of the Adriatic; mandated standalone per global constraints.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Friuli-Venezia Giulia NUTS-2 ITH4

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Trieste — former Habsburg imperial port, insurance/finance hub with a distinctive Central European character
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: port logistics, insurance (Generali), furniture manufacturing (Udine), shipbuilding/marine tech
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: special-statute autonomy reflecting Friulian and Slovene minority presence, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Trieste's port and Central European trade links give strong transportation self-sufficiency; Friulian plain agriculture supports moderate food self-sufficiency for a small special-statute region.

rationales.water: Friulian plain rivers and Alpine headwaters give ample supply for a small population.
rationales.food: Friulian-plain agriculture supports moderate self-sufficiency for a small special-statute region.
rationales.energy: Trieste's port/trade role is not matched by domestic generation; net importer.

pole.note: Trieste: port/political capital; Udine: inland historic Friulian cultural capital.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale del Friuli Venezia Giulia
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 ITH (Nord-Est) groups South Tyrol with Trentino, Veneto, and Friuli; separated here as its own congruent-variant unit given its distinct German-speaking special-autonomy status.
regions.name: South Tyrol
regions.identity_basis: German-speaking majority special-autonomy province (Austrian until 1918); congruent (Italy-only) variant of the Tyrol toggle group. The unified Tyrol record (joining Austrian Tirol) lives in zone1.json.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ASTAT), Provincia Autonoma di Bolzano/Bozen NUTS-2 ITH1

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bolzano/Bozen — provincial capital, German-Italian bilingual administrative and cultural hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Alpine tourism (Dolomites UNESCO site), apple and wine agriculture, precision manufacturing, hydropower
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: German-speaking majority with full linguistic-cultural autonomy within Italy, an option for Austrian dual citizenship since 2023, historically contested but not currently secessionist

autarky.rationale: Abundant Alpine water and extensive hydropower generation give the highest water and energy scores in the Italian set; mountainous terrain constrains transportation connectivity relative to lowland regions.

rationales.water: Abundant Alpine snowmelt gives the highest water score in the Italian set.
rationales.food: Apple/wine agriculture is strong per capita despite mountainous terrain limiting total arable area.
rationales.energy: Extensive hydropower gives South Tyrol a rare energy-positive position in this dataset.

sources: South Tyrol special-autonomy statute and Austria dual-citizenship provisions (2023)

parliament.name: Landtag Südtirol / Consiglio della Provincia autonoma di Bolzano
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.name: Trentino
regions.identity_basis: Italian-speaking special-autonomy province, historically and linguistically distinct from German-speaking South Tyrol despite sharing the joint Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol regional structure; mandated standalone per zone brief.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISPAT), Provincia Autonoma di Trento NUTS-2 ITH2

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Trento — provincial capital and university/research hub (University of Trento)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Alpine tourism, apple/wine agriculture, hydropower, ICT/research (FBK research foundation)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Italian-speaking Trentino identity, special autonomy status, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Shares South Tyrol's Alpine water and hydropower abundance; slightly stronger ICT/research diversification via the Trento university-research cluster offsets otherwise similar mountain-region constraints.

rationales.water: Shares South Tyrol's Alpine snowmelt abundance.
rationales.food: Apple/wine agriculture on Alpine valley floors gives solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Hydropower generation is comparably strong to South Tyrol's.

sources: ISPAT (Istituto di Statistica della Provincia di Trento)

parliament.name: Consiglio della Provincia autonoma di Trento
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 ITH5 (Emilia-Romagna) treats Emilia and Romagna as one administrative region; split here per the mandated Emilia≠Romagna decision. Ferrara (ITH56) is assigned to Emilia rather than Romagna based on Pellegrini's dialect classification placing Ferrarese within the Emiliano group, though Ferrara's historical inclusion in the Papal Legations alongside Ravenna and Forlì is a genuine competing frame — flagged in zone notes for the methodology page.
regions.name: Emilia
regions.identity_basis: Western half of Emilia-Romagna, distinguished from Romagna by the Emiliano dialect group (Pellegrini's Carta dei dialetti d'Italia classifies Ferrara's dialect as Emiliano, not Romagnolo, despite Ferrara's historical Papal-Legation administrative pairing with Ravenna); food-industry and automotive 'Motor Valley' heartland.
key_industries: food processing (Parmigiano-Reggiano, Prosciutto di Parma, balsamic vinegar)
regions.population_note: Eurostat/ISTAT 2023 estimate, sum of NUTS-3 provinces Piacenza+Parma+Reggio Emilia+Modena+Bologna+Ferrara (ITH51-ITH56)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bologna — metro ~1M, historic university city (oldest in the Western world) and Emilian cultural-culinary capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: world-renowned food-processing PDO/PGI clusters, 'Motor Valley' luxury automotive and motorsport, packaging machinery, biomedical devices
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Emilian dialect and food-culture identity, no separatism, mandated split from Romagna per project brief

autarky.rationale: Extraordinarily high food self-sufficiency and export strength (Po Valley agriculture plus globally famous PDO food clusters); diversified high-value manufacturing (automotive, packaging machinery, biomedical) gives strong industrial resilience across most dimensions.

rationales.water: Po Valley aquifers and Apennine headwaters give reliable supply for intensive agri-food processing.
rationales.food: World-renowned PDO food clusters (Parmigiano-Reggiano, Prosciutto di Parma) give the dataset's highest food scores.
rationales.energy: Diversified manufacturing (automotive, packaging) is energy-intensive; moderate domestic generation only partly offsets it.

sources: Pellegrini, G.B. (1977) Carta dei dialetti d'Italia — Emiliano/Romagnolo dialect boundary

parliament.name: Assemblea legislativa dell'Emilia-Romagna (shared with Romagna)
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.nuts1_disagreement: See Emilia record for the shared NUTS-2 ITH5 disagreement and the Ferrara assignment reasoning.
regions.name: Romagna
regions.identity_basis: Eastern half of Emilia-Romagna, distinguished by the Romagnolo dialect group and a historically separate identity from Emilia (Byzantine Exarchate of Ravenna origin of the name 'Romagna' = 'land of the Romans/Byzantines', vs. Lombard-ruled Emilia); mandated split per project brief.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/ISTAT 2023 estimate, sum of NUTS-3 provinces Ravenna+Forlì-Cesena+Rimini (ITH57-ITH59)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Ravenna — former Western Roman and Byzantine imperial capital (UNESCO mosaics), Adriatic port; Rimini as mass-tourism hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Adriatic beach tourism (Rimini/Riccione), fruit-and-vegetable food processing, Faenza ceramics (origin of the word 'faience'), Ravenna port and petrochemical complex
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Romagnolo dialect and post-Byzantine historical identity, culturally proud regionalism ('Romagna, terra di...') but no separatism

autarky.rationale: Adriatic coast tourism and food-processing agriculture give solid but slightly lower composite than Emilia, reflecting smaller scale and heavier tourism-seasonality dependence relative to Emilia's diversified manufacturing base.

rationales.water: Adriatic coastal aquifers are adequate but seasonal tourism spikes demand sharply.
rationales.food: Fruit/vegetable canning and Adriatic fishing give solid, if smaller-scale than Emilia's, self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Ravenna's petrochemical/port complex is a significant local energy user with only partial domestic offset.

sources: Pellegrini, G.B. (1977) Carta dei dialetti d'Italia; Romagna historical-identity literature (Exarchate of Ravenna)

pole.note: Ravenna is historic capital (Byzantine Exarchate); Rimini is the larger economic/tourism center — genuinely polycentric.

parliament.name: Assemblea legislativa dell'Emilia-Romagna (shared with Emilia)
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Tuscany
regions.identity_basis: Cradle of the Italian Renaissance and of standard Italian itself (Tuscan dialect basis of modern Italian); historic Grand Duchy of Tuscany; globally recognized cultural-agricultural identity (Chianti, Renaissance art cities).
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Toscana NUTS-2 ITI1

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Florence — metro ~1M, Renaissance capital and UNESCO World Heritage city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: textiles (Prato's large manufacturing district, including a major Chinese-Italian textile cluster), wine, leather/fashion, pharma/vaccine research (Siena)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Tuscan identity and the historical origin of standard Italian, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Chianti/Maremma agriculture and viticulture support strong food self-sufficiency; Prato's textile district gives above-average clothing self-sufficiency relative to most other Italian regions in this dataset.

rationales.water: Arno-basin and Apennine supply is generally reliable outside drought years.
rationales.food: Chianti/Maremma viticulture and agriculture give strong self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Larderello geothermal field gives Tuscany a genuine (if regionally concentrated) domestic generation source.

sources: Tuscan Renaissance and dialect-standardization literature (Bembo's codification of Tuscan)

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Toscana
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Umbria
regions.identity_basis: Italy's only landlocked peninsular region south of the Alps, self-styled 'the green heart of Italy'; distinct Umbrian identity predating Roman conquest (ancient Umbri people); assessed and retained per inclusion test.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Umbria NUTS-2 ITI2

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Perugia — regional capital, university city (Università per Stranieri), chocolate-industry headquarters
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: steel manufacturing (Terni), confectionery (Perugina/Nestlé), olive oil and Sagrantino wine, pilgrimage/cultural tourism (Assisi)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct pre-Roman Umbrian identity and 'green heart of Italy' self-image, no separatism; assessed against the inclusion test and retained as a clear pass

autarky.rationale: Landlocked but water-rich (Alpine-fed rivers, Trasimeno basin) with strong olive-oil/wine agriculture; smaller scale and hillier terrain than Tuscany moderate transportation and industrial-diversification scores slightly.

rationales.water: Landlocked but water-rich via Alpine-fed rivers and the Trasimeno basin.
rationales.food: Olive oil and Sagrantino-wine agriculture support strong self-sufficiency for a small region.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation source; net importer via the national grid.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale dell'Umbria
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Marche
regions.identity_basis: Adriatic-facing region named for the medieval marches (border marks) of the Holy Roman Empire; distinctive dense small-and-medium-enterprise manufacturing model ('Marche model') and its own dialect continuum; assessed and retained per inclusion test.

autarky.rationale: Atlantic-facing agriculture/forestry and a diversified manufacturing base (ceramics, glass, paper) give solid, unremarkable-but-adequate scores across most dimensions, consistent with the region's real character as a productive but less internationally distinctive part of mainland Portugal.

rationales.water: Atlantic-facing river basins (Mondego, Vouga) give reliable, unremarkable supply.
rationales.food: Forestry, Bairrada viticulture, and mixed agriculture give solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation; ceramics/glass/paper manufacturing draws on the national grid.

conflict_flags.description: Historically, Comunidad de Madrid was carved out of 'New Castile'/La Mancha territory (formalized 1833, autonomous community 1983). This composite deliberately excludes Madrid to preserve the site's Catalonia-Madrid flagship framing; a historically 'fuller' Castile would include it. Flagged rather than silently resolved.

regions.name: Greater Castile (unified)
regions.identity_basis: Non-congruent composite union of León(Castile) + La Mancha(Castile) — i.e. the historic 'Old Castile' (Castilla la Vieja, NUTS-2 ES41) plus 'New Castile' (Castilla la Nueva, NUTS-2 ES42) — representing the pre-1833-provincial-reform, pre-Madrid-secession idea of a single Castilian cultural bloc. Comunidad de Madrid (ES30) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED even though it was historically carved out of New Castile/La Mancha in 1833: Madrid is authored as its own flagship capital-region unit (monopole, site-framing counterweight to Catalonia) and reuniting it here would contradict that mandate and the map's Catalonia-Madrid tension example. This is the 'connected' view of the leon-castile variant set.
regions.population_note: Sum of es-castile-leon (ES41, ~2,383,000) + es-castile-la-mancha (ES42, ~2,050,000); non-default composite, Madrid (ES30) deliberately excluded.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Valladolid (largest city of the union) — no single unified capital exists for this composite
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: combined cereal/wine agriculture, automotive manufacturing across both member territories
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: represents a historical pan-Castilian identity frame rather than a governing reality; both member Autonomous Communities retain their own separate statutes and parliaments

parliament.note: Non-governing composite; the two member Autonomous Communities each retain their own real parliament (Cortes de Castilla y León, Cortes de Castilla-La Mancha).

autarky.rationale: Combines two high-food-autarky cereal/wine plateaus; scores approximate the population-weighted average of the two member records.

rationales.water: Combines two plateau basins (Duero + Mancha aquifer); adequate on average though the Mancha side is structurally over-exploited.
rationales.food: Combines two of the dataset's highest-food-scoring records (cereal breadbasket + wine plain).
rationales.energy: Combines Castile-León's wind buildout with Castile-La Mancha's solar buildout for a solidly positive composite.

conflict_flags.description: Using full NUTS-3 provinces (Segovia, Ávila, Guadalajara, Toledo) rather than finer municipal/comarca geometry means this record includes large rural areas of each province far outside any realistic daily-commute shed of Madrid. No finer NUTS geometry is available in the index; flagged rather than silently corrected, matching the existing basque-unified/FRI15 precedent.

regions.name: Madrid & Surroundings
regions.identity_basis: Extended commuter-belt variant of Madrid, reaching into the nearest NUTS-3 provinces of both neighboring Castiles that function as Madrid's daily-commuter/exurban catchment: Segovia (ES416) and Ávila (ES411) from Castile-León to the northwest, Guadalajara (ES424) and Toledo (ES425) from Castile-La Mancha to the east/south. Codes are deliberately at NUTS-3 (province) granularity, not the coarser NUTS-2 Autonomous Community level, to avoid grossly overstating the commuter belt by annexing entire neighboring regions. This is the 'with-surroundings' view of the madrid variant set.
regions.population_note: Comunidad de Madrid (ES300, ~6,751,000) + approximate combined population of the four bordering commuter-belt NUTS-3 provinces (Segovia+Ávila+Guadalajara+Toledo, order-of-magnitude ~150,000-800,000 depending on how much of each large, mostly-rural province is actually within Madrid's functional commute-shed; not independently reconciled against province-level Eurostat tables in this pass, flagged for verification).

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Madrid — same national-capital hub as the congruent es-madrid record
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: same as es-madrid, plus the surrounding provinces' logistics/warehousing and agri-food capacity
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: functional commuter-belt extension, not a distinct identity claim; represents Madrid's real metropolitan-region gravity beyond the Comunidad de Madrid's own administrative boundary

parliament.note: Non-governing composite; Madrid retains its own Asamblea, the bordering provinces belong to Castile-León/Castile-La Mancha's respective parliaments.

autarky.rationale: Adding four largely rural/agricultural provinces to Madrid's core slightly raises food self-sufficiency relative to the congruent record; transport/healthcare remain capital-region-dominated scores.

rationales.water: Adds four largely rural provinces' catchments to Madrid's reservoir system; modest net improvement.
rationales.food: Adding rural/agricultural provinces slightly raises food self-sufficiency relative to the congruent Madrid record.
rationales.energy: Still dominated by Madrid's own import-dependent profile; the added provinces contribute little generation capacity.

sources: Comunidad de Madrid regional statistics office
